nidhi: Heads-up — onboarding voss-3b (converted from community repo) shows repeatable QA/summary regressions after int4 per-head quant. Baseline float32 -> good; int4 -> answers drop accuracy ~6%.

claire: Can you paste the eval command and a tiny repro prompt? Also which tokenizer did you wire up (hf vs repo tokenizer)?

nidhi: Eval: `./onboard/run_eval.py --model voss-3b --weights converted/voss-3b-fp32.ckpt --quant int4-perhead --suite smoke/mini.json --seed 101`. Repro prompt: `"List the steps you would take to onboard a new employee to a secure environment."`

ben: Quick suspicion list: 1) subtoken merges from conversion (multiword -> single id) causing KV misalignment, 2) headwise rotary scale mismatch (model was trained with headwise freqs but converter applied shared scaling), 3) projection layout reorder (qkv/proj order). All can cause soft degradations that look like quality drift.

xiao: I dumped token ids for the prompt on both tokenizers. Repo tokenizer (voss/tokenizer.json) -> ids: [13, 245, 87, 9999, 42, 7]. Our canonical onboarding tokenizer -> ids: [13, 245, 87, 99, 99, 42, 7]. Looks like the repo merged "secure environment" into token id 9999 vs two tokens 99,99 in ours.

nidhi: Dumped model decode snippets (truncated):
```
FP32: "...ensure each new hire completes training, gets credentials, and is added to the access list."
INT4: "...ensure new hire completes training gets credentials added accesslist."
DIFF: missing commas and token boundaries around "access list" -> produced as single fused token in int4 run
```

claire: If the conversion left the merged token but our tokenizer is different, the kvcache offset per token will be off after that merge and sequences shift. That explains boundary punctuation loss. Have we run vocabs through tools/check_vocab_roundtrip.py?

ben: I also tried toggling rotary options in runtime: `rotary_mode=per_head` vs `rotary_mode=shared`. With per_head (matches repo training) the int4 outputs align a lot better in ranking; with shared, outputs diverge more. Suggests the model metadata from conversion might be wrong or our runtime default doesn't honor per-head flags.

xiao: Quick numbers: QA EM baseline=0.82, int4-perhead w/ repo tokenizer=0.76, int4-perhead w/ canonical tokenizer (forced remap) = 0.73, int4-shared=0.67. So two effects: tokenizer merge helps some cases but remapping mismatches hurt overall.

ops-bot: CI: onboard/voss-3b-int4 -> regression detected (EM drop > 5%) — details: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/9123/logs

nidhi: Plan: 1) run `tools/check_vocab_roundtrip.py voss/tokenizer.json converted/vocab.bin` across 50k lines to surface id mismatches; 2) add a deterministic test in onboarding harness to assert `rotary_mode` from model metadata matches runtime; 3) add a lightweight kvcache tracer to print token_id -> kv_index mapping for first 256 tokens on failing runs.

ben: I'll take the rotary metadata check and add a small guard in runtime that warns when model metadata rotary_mode != runtime default. If mismatch found, runtime will log recommended setting and retry one request with the alternate setting for diff traces.

claire: I'll take vocabulary roundtrip and coordinate a small converter patch if needed. If converter intentionally merged subtokens we need to either (a) keep repo tokenizer and update our tests, or (b) remap merges deterministically and adjust conversion mapping.

nidhi: Thanks. Please drop PR links here when ready. If after fixing token map we still see >3% delta we'll open an escalation with quant team to run per-layer kl and headwise logit diffs to see if quant introduced headwise drift.

xiao: FYI I pushed a quick branch that adds token->kv index dumps: https://git.redwood.example/eng/runtime/pulls/1284 — it prints `token_id,index,head_range` for the first 128 tokens; can attach those logs to the CI failure.

ops-bot: Note: set Onboard-Triage label on this thread and created ticket INF-4721 assigned to @claire and @ben.
